name: Stonewake Museum

text: THE AURELIAN CASE.
Eleven pieces of worked metal, none of them from a mine anyone can name.
The card says: FOUND IN CAELORA. MAKERS UNKNOWN. AGE UNKNOWN.
A disc the size of a saucer, cut with circles inside circles
and a spiral running out of the middle of them.
Whatever it was, somebody made it to be looked at closely.
A rubbing taken from a wall somewhere out in the forest.
People. Kin standing beside them, not behind them. Then the sea.
Then a shape too big for the paper, and the rubbing stops.
The stone gallery. Forty kinds of rock out of one mountain,
each with the name of the man who first cut it under the label.
Nine of them are Quills.
Kin of the high country: bones, casts, and one very cross-looking
stuffed Gravelet from a century when people did that.
A modern card beside it apologises, at some length.
A plinth: the first cart wheel off the Stonewake tramway.
Iron, worn oval, and heavier than it looks.
Everyone tries to lift it. There is a small notice asking you not to.
A plinth of survey instruments, brass and glass, donated this year.
The donor plate reads: THE MERIDIAN FOUNDATION.
It is the newest thing in the building by about ninety years.
Shelf after shelf of pit records. Shift books, wage books, inquests.
Somebody has been reading the inquests. There is a bookmark in one.
The bookmark is a Hall challenger's ticket, four years out of date.
The drowned galleries, in photographs taken before the pumps went.
Water standing black and perfectly still in a worked-out chamber.
The card notes that the level has not changed since spring.
A model of Stonewake before the terrace was cut: forty houses,
one road, and a mountain nobody had put a mark on yet.
A visitors' book. The last four pages are the same handwriting
on four different days, asking the same question in the comments column:
WHO ELSE HAS ASKED ABOUT THE DISC

_plan: One long hall, because a museum the player has to navigate is a museum they leave. The Aurelian case is the far wall, so Lyra is the first person you walk towards. Everything else in the room is Stonewake talking about itself -- rock, pit records, drowned galleries -- which is what makes the one case of unexplained metal stand out without a single line of dialogue pointing at it.
